thesis: In July 2024, Jalen Brunson signed a four-year, $156.5M extension with the Knicks—$113M less than the five-year, $269.1M max deal available in 2025—preserving salary cap flexibility and keeping the team below the punitive second apron threshold.

facts.claim: Brunson signed a four-year, $156.5 million veteran extension in July 2024, declining a five-year, $269.1 million max contract eligible in 2025.
The extension generated $37.1 million in future salary cap savings for the Knicks, providing relief from the second-apron payroll threshold.
Brunson's deal includes a fourth-year player option for 2028-29, allowing him to recoup forgone earnings via a $323M four-year or $418M five-year extension.
The extension keeps Brunson's salary below 23 percent of the salary cap annually, maintaining financial flexibility throughout the deal's duration.
By staying below the second apron, the Knicks retain full flexibility to trade, sign free agents and use draft picks—benefits blocked at the second-apron level.
Brunson's sacrifice mirrored championship-organization contract models, citing Patrick Mahomes' Chiefs, Tom Brady's Patriots and Derek Jeter's Yankees as structural blueprints.
